The amnestic definition requires that episode amnesia status be documented: 97 percent of the located clinical cohort had partial or total amnesia, so the behaviour and any mood effect it produces are separated in time by an interval the patient frequently cannot recall, and no individual attribution may rest on the patient's own account of the episodes.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Depressive symptoms are the most consistently reported psychological finding in sleep-related eating disorder, and the located cross-sectional evidence quantifies both the prevalence and the elevation. A study administering the Inventory of Nocturnal Eating, a self-report questionnaire addressing nocturnal eating and sleep disturbance, to out-patients with eating disorders (N = 126), in-patients with eating disorders (N = 24), obese subjects in a trial of an anorexic agent (N = 126), depressed subjects in an antidepressant trial (N = 207) and an unselected group of college students (N = 217), for a total of 700, operationally defining sleep-related eating disorder as nocturnal eating with a self-reported REDUCED LEVEL OF AWARENESS occurring at least once per week, found that ALMOST 5.0 PERCENT (33 OF 700) described symptoms consistent with the syndrome, that the in-patient eating disorders group had nearly twice the prevalence (16.7 percent) of the out-patient sample (8.7 percent) which had nearly twice the prevalence of the student sample (4.6 percent), and that SUBJECTS WITH SLEEP-RELATED EATING DISORDER ENDORSED MORE SYMPTOMS CONSISTENT WITH SLEEP DISORDERS AND HAD HIGHER LEVELS OF DEPRESSION AND DISSOCIATION THAN THOSE WITHOUT NOCTURNAL EATING, concluding that sleep disorder symptoms are often associated with sleep-related eating disorder, as are depression and dissociation (PMID 10616953). A descriptive study of 34 consecutive adults meeting International Classification of Sleep Disorders criteria for sleep-related eating disorder who did NOT meet DSM-IV criteria for an eating disorder, in whom 97 percent had partial or total amnesia of episodes, found comorbidities that were FREQUENT AND INCLUDED INSOMNIA IN 58.8 PERCENT, RESTLESS LEGS SYNDROME IN 47 PERCENT, SLEEP-DISORDERED BREATHING IN 26 PERCENT, AND PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS IN 38.2 PERCENT, with a mean latency from symptom onset to diagnosis of 8.3 years (PMID 24424097). A systematic literature review of the exploration of sleep-related eating disorder records the importance of this pathology and its NEGATIVE FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCES (PMID 38873533). Recorded as documented association only, with the cross-sectional nature of the primary anchor and the amnestic nature of the episodes both carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence cannot establish temporal order for a reason internal to the disorder itself. Sleep-related eating disorder is defined by PARTIAL OR TOTAL AMNESIA for the eating episodes in 97 percent of the located clinical cohort, so the eating behaviour and any mood symptoms it produces are separated in time by an intervening period of amnesia, which means the very experience that might plausibly worsen mood is frequently not remembered by the patient and may not even be reported (PMID 24424097). The primary anchor is CROSS-SECTIONAL and its direction is ambiguous by construction: it enrolled DEPRESSED SUBJECTS in an antidepressant trial and then found higher depression scores among those with sleep-related eating, so depression may precede the disorder, follow it, or share a cause, and the anchor's own design cannot separate those (PMID 10616953). The second anchor is a descriptive single-centre case series of 34 patients who were specifically selected for having NO daytime eating disorder, so its psychiatric comorbidity figure describes a subgroup that is unrepresentative of the disorder's common overlap with daytime eating disorders (PMID 24424097). Individual claims require a dated sleep-related eating disorder diagnosis with episode frequency and amnesia status documented, a dated depressive-disorder diagnosis, and a clinical determination of which is antecedent, together with a separate screen for a daytime eating disorder, because the located prevalence gradient runs from 4.6 percent in students to 8.7 percent in out-patient and 16.7 percent in in-patient eating-disorder samples, meaning the majority of located cases are people who already carry a daytime eating disorder.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is that the episodes occur out of conscious control during partial arousal and are typically not remembered, so the patient wakes to unexplained food, to disrupted sleep, and frequently to a partner or family member who witnessed the behaviour, leaving an intrusive and shame-laden residue that the patient cannot narrate to their own satisfaction, which is a recognised route to low mood; a second and more directly evidenced vector is that the underlying depression disrupts sleep and appetite regulation and thereby produces nocturnal eating. The two vectors run in OPPOSITE directions, which is why the edge names them together and why the conservative standard requires a temporal determination rather than assuming the first.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at cross-sectional-questionnaire-survey, descriptive-case-series, and systematic-literature-review class, following the file's existing psychiatric, eating-behaviour, and sleep-related pathway scope. The cross-sectional survey is the anchor and supplies both the prevalence estimate of 5.0 percent in 700 subjects and the prevalence GRADIENT across populations, from 4.6 percent in students to 8.7 percent in out-patient and 16.7 percent in in-patient eating-disorder samples, which is what establishes that this disorder is mostly a feature of people who already have a daytime eating disorder and is the located reason the co-occurring depression cannot be read as caused by the nocturnal eating alone (PMID 10616953). The clinical case series is the anchor that supplies the comorbidity profile, insomnia in 58.8 percent, restless legs syndrome in 47 percent, sleep-disordered breathing in 26 percent, psychiatric disorders in 38.2 percent, and the 8.3-year mean latency from onset to diagnosis, together with the amnestic definition (PMID 24424097). The systematic review is registered as the weakest reference class in this edge and is disclosed as such, supplying the framing of negative functional consequences without a quantified outcome (PMID 38873533). Because the located evidence is cross-sectional and the disorder is amnestic by definition, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, names both directional vectors, and requires a daytime eating-disorder screen before attribution.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary anchor is CROSS-SECTIONAL and enrolled DEPRESSED SUBJECTS IN AN ANTICIPRESSANT TRIAL among its five comparison groups, so the direction of the association between the nocturnal eating and the depressive scores is unresolvable from its own design, and its instrument is a SELF-REPORT QUESTIONNAIRE with an operational definition requiring only self-reported reduced awareness and weekly frequency (PMID 10616953). The second anchor is a 34-patient single-centre DESCRIPTIVE case series of patients specifically selected for NOT having a daytime eating disorder, so its 38.2 percent psychiatric comorbidity figure describes precisely the minority group in whom the co-occurring daytime disorder is absent, and it reports comorbidity presence rather than any measured severity or a mood instrument score for this edge (PMID 24424097). The third anchor is a systematic literature review that is FRAMING RATHER THAN QUANTIFYING, being a single-author narrative review of current evidence and future perspectives that supplies no pooled estimate and no outcome data, and it is the weakest reference class in this edge and is retained only because the located evidence base for this disorder is genuinely thin (PMID 38873533). NO located anchor establishes that treating the nocturnal eating reduces depressive symptoms, and none reports depressive-disorder incidence in an unselected population with this disorder.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: A co-existing daytime eating disorder, which the located prevalence gradient places in the majority of cases and which must be documented because it changes the direction of the mood relationship entirely

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Anxiety and dissociative symptoms accompany the nocturnal eating in the located cross-sectional evidence, and dissociative symptom burden in particular is named alongside depression. A questionnaire survey of 700 subjects across five clinical and non-clinical groups, operationally defining sleep-related eating disorder as nocturnal eating with a self-reported reduced level of awareness occurring at least once per week, found that ALMOST 5.0 PERCENT (33 OF 700) described symptoms consistent with the syndrome, that the in-patient eating disorders group had nearly twice the prevalence (16.7 percent) of the out-patient sample (8.7 percent) and nearly twice that of the student sample (4.6 percent), and that SUBJECTS WITH SLEEP-RELATED EATING DISORDER ENDORSED MORE SYMPTOMS CONSISTENT WITH SLEEP DISORDERS AND HAD HIGHER LEVELS OF DEPRESSION AND DISSOCIATION THAN THOSE WITHOUT NOCTURNAL EATING, concluding that sleep disorder symptoms are often associated with sleep-related eating disorder, as are depression and dissociation (PMID 10616953). A descriptive study of 34 consecutive adults meeting International Classification of Sleep Disorders criteria for the disorder who did not meet daytime eating-disorder criteria found FREQUENT COMORBIDITIES INCLUDING INSOMNIA IN 58.8 PERCENT, RESTLESS LEGS SYNDROME IN 47 PERCENT, SLEEP-DISORDERED BREATHING IN 26 PERCENT AND PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS IN 38.2 PERCENT, in a population where 97 percent had partial or total amnesia of the episodes and the mean latency from symptom onset to diagnosis was 8.3 years (PMID 24424097). A case-control study of 21 adolescents with sleep terrors or sleepwalking found statistically significant differences in overanxious disorder, panic disorder and simple phobia between cases and controls, establishing that the arousal-parasomnia family this disorder belongs to carries named anxiety diagnoses in an adolescent population (PMID 10544999). Recorded as documented association only, with the substitution of a sibling-identity anchor disclosed rather than presented as direct evidence.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and this edge rests on a WEAKER EVIDENTIARY BASE THAN ITS RANK SUGGESTS, which is why it is ranked second. The two direct anchors report psychiatric DISORDERS and DEPRESSION AND DISSOCIATION, not diagnosed anxiety disorders: the primary anchor reports elevated scores on depression and dissociation rather than anxiety (PMID 10616953), and the second reports the presence of psychiatric disorders in 38.2 percent without specifying their composition (PMID 24424097). The third anchor does NOT STUDY THIS IDENTITY AT ALL. It studies sleep terrors and sleepwalking, the sibling arousal parasomnias, and is registered here only because it is the located source that names overanxious disorder, panic disorder and simple phobia in this disorder family; using it as an anchor for a sleep-related eating disorder claim requires an inference across identities that no located anchor makes, and that inference is stated here rather than buried. Dissociation, which the primary anchor does report, is itself notable because the amnestic definition of the disorder and the dissociative symptom elevation may be two descriptions of the same partial-arousal phenomenon, so dissociation is named in the alternatives rather than treated as independent evidence of an anxiety disorder. Individual claims require a dated sleep-related eating disorder diagnosis, a dated anxiety-disorder diagnosis with a named instrument, and a clinical determination of which is antecedent, together with a screen for a daytime eating disorder, depression, dissociation, restless legs syndrome and sleep-disordered breathing, all of which the located cohorts report at substantial rates.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is that partial arousal from sleep during which the patient eats without retained awareness is itself a dissociative state, so that the experience of unaccounted-for eating, unaccounted-for food in the home, and a partner's account of behaviour the patient does not remember produces anticipatory hypervigilance about the next episode, and the hypervigilance is the most plausible route to an anxiety presentation; a second vector runs in the opposite direction, in which an anxiety disorder disrupts sleep continuity and the arousal threshold that ordinarily prevents eating behaviour emerging from sleep. The two vectors are named together because the located evidence reports co-occurrence without direction, and because the amnestic definition of the disorder means the patient's own account of the episodes, which is what an anxiety account would rest on, is frequently unavailable.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at cross-sectional-questionnaire-survey, descriptive-case-series, and small-case-control class, following the file's existing psychiatric, eating-behaviour, and sleep-related pathway scope. The cross-sectional survey is the anchor and supplies the prevalence estimate and the population gradient, and it is the located source that names DISSOCIATION alongside depression, which is the finding that most directly supports a psychological rather than purely behavioural account of this edge (PMID 10616953). The clinical case series is the anchor that supplies the comorbidity profile and the amnestic definition (PMID 24424097). The sibling case-control study is registered as a SIBLING-IDENTITY ANCHOR and its substitution is disclosed in the anchor's own note and in the evidence gaps, because the located literature names anxiety diagnoses in sleepwalking and sleep terror but not in this disorder, and using it here is an explicit inference across related identities (PMID 10544999). Because the direct anchors report psychiatric disorders and dissociation rather than anxiety diagnoses, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, ranks it below the mood edge, and requires a named anxiety instrument for any individual claim.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: NO ANCHOR IN THIS EDGE REPORTS A DIAGNOSED ANXIETY DISORDER IN A POPULATION WITH THIS DISORDER. The primary anchor reports DEPRESSION AND DISSOCIATION scores, not anxiety, and dissociation in a disorder defined by partial arousal may be the same phenomenon rather than a separate anxiety presentation (PMID 10616953). The second anchor reports PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS IN 38.2 PERCENT without specifying composition, and it is a 34-patient descriptive series deliberately restricted to patients WITHOUT a daytime eating disorder, so it describes the minority of cases (PMID 24424097). The third anchor DOES NOT STUDY THIS IDENTITY: it studies sleep terrors and sleepwalking, and its final analysed group is 21 cases against 30 controls using a translated paediatric instrument (PMID 10544999). This is the weakest anchor alignment in the batch and it is the reason the edge is ranked second and why the evidence gaps state that no direct anxiety anchor was located. NO located anchor establishes that treating the nocturnal eating reduces anxiety, and none reports anxiety-disorder incidence in an unselected population with this disorder.

governanceNotes: D1 batch 85 (2026-09-27): two bounded associations authored in draft quarantine, and the defining feature of this file is that it is the only file in the batch where one of the two edges is built on an anchor that does not study the identity. That substitution is disclosed in three places rather than concealed, because a reviewer reading only the reference list would otherwise reasonably assume the anxiety evidence was gathered in this population.

A SIBLING CHECK WAS PERFORMED AND REPORTED across the four identities in mental-disorders-expansion-wave-6.json. The four are GENUINELY DISTINCT, and the located evidence treats sleep-related eating disorder as a discrete parasomnia rather than a variant of the others, but the sleepwalking and sleep terror tension recorded on those files applies here too: the located clinical literature groups these events under the broader parasomnia and disorder-of-arousal categories, so this catalog is finer-grained than the clinical literature and the edges are written accordingly.

THE THIRD REFERENCE ON BOTH EDGES OF THIS FILE IS THE WEAKEST CLASS IN THE BATCH AND IS LABELLED AS SUCH. A single-author narrative review of current evidence and future perspectives, which supplies no pooled estimate, no measured mood outcome and no comparison group, is retained on the mood edge because the located evidence base for this disorder is genuinely thin, and the note on that reference says plainly that it is the weakest reference class in the edge rather than presenting it as equivalent to the two prospective studies beside it.

WITHHELD ROUTES: obesity as MISSING IDENTITY, which is the single most clinically significant association in the located literature, where disordered eating and obesity are reported together and where the primary anchor enrolled obese subjects specifically, but NO CATALOG IDENTITY FOR OBESITY EXISTS, so the route cannot be authored and is recorded as a continuing catalog gap alongside the obesity and metabolic syndrome gaps already carried from earlier batches. binge-eating-disorder and rumination-syndrome as SEPARATE-CATALOG-IDENTITIES with the REVERSE DIRECTION, both being daytime eating disorders that the located prevalence gradient shows are the setting in which this disorder most often appears, so the arrows run from them to this one. restless-legs-syndrome and sleep-apnea as SHARED-AND-REVERSED, the located clinical cohort reporting restless legs syndrome in 47 percent and sleep-disordered breathing in 26 percent, both of which produce the nocturnal arousal that precedes the episodes and both of which are plausible antecedents rather than consequences. psychiatric-disorder as UMBRELLA, the located case series reporting psychiatric disorders in 38.2 percent without composition.

Catalog gap recorded without numbering: the located literature describes medication-induced sleep-related eating-like behaviour, including the well-described association with sedatives, antipsychotics and certain antidepressants, and no catalog identity exists for a medication-induced eating behaviour; recorded for a future batch rather than numbered as a refusal, since the disposition here is identity scope rather than a decision about the evidence.
